title: The Table That Describes an Arm: Denavit-Hartenberg Rows, Two Conventions, and the Same Numbers That Are Two Different Arms

questions.question: A vendor gives a Denavit-Hartenberg table. What else must you know to use it?
options: Which convention it was written for: standard and modified are different arms for the same numbers
questions.explanation: One table gave tools 0.626211 m apart.

questions.question: What is the standard convention for one row?
questions.explanation: The modified is Rx Tx Rz Tz.

questions.question: A joint slides. Where does its variable go?
options: Into d: it is added to the offset along z

questions.question: Why does a SCARA table have a twist of pi on its second row?
options: It flips z, so that the slide of the third joint goes down

questions.question: A flat table with no twists and no offsets, in the two conventions. Same arm?
options: No: 0.244589 m apart for these angles
questions.explanation: The modified convention puts the length before the angle.

questions.question: The joint variables are all zero and there are no twists or offsets. Do the conventions agree?
options: Yes: the links are laid end to end along x
